title: BERT and GPT Style Language Models
overview: Pretrained transformer language models learn from large text corpora. BERT-style encoders predict masked tokens for understanding tasks, while GPT-style decoders predict the next token for generation.
objectives: Contrast masked and causal language modeling
Explain pretraining followed by fine-tuning or prompting

method.title: Encoder models
method.body: BERT-style models use bidirectional attention and a masked-token objective, producing contextual embeddings for classification and tagging.

method.title: Decoder models
method.body: GPT-style models use causal attention and are trained to predict the next token, which also enables text generation.

method.title: Tokenization
method.body: Subword tokenizers split text into pieces so rare words are still representable.

method.title: Decoding
method.body: Generation can use greedy, beam search, or sampling with temperature and top-k or top-p.

pseudocode:
# causal LM loss
logits = model(tokens[:, :-1])
loss = cross_entropy(logits, tokens[:, 1:])
# sampling
p = softmax(logits[-1] / temperature)
next = sample(p)

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
logits = np.array([2.0, 1.0, 0.2, -1.0])
vocab = ["the", "cat", "sat", "mat"]
for T in (0.5, 1.0, 2.0):
    p = np.exp(logits / T); p /= p.sum()
    print("T=%.1f" % T, dict(zip(vocab, np.round(p, 2).tolist())))
